description: The thread draft's policy: K = S* = a million 20-bit tokens, Gamma = 2 N D for a 1M-token session at 32B active parameters. Kimi K2 shapes: 32B active of 1.04T parameters, d_model 7168, routed-expert width 2048, 61 layers. Assumes a public cap on the committed parameters' size, a few times the largest permitted model, proved inside the zero-knowledge proof, so no noise tables or corpora of that size can be committed.

The same policy with no cap on the committed parameters' size, as the policy stands today: a developer may commit a noise table (one entry per parameter per direction), so seed-based decoding costs one multiply-add per parameter per direction instead of a PRNG draw.

The same sessions with prompts arithmetic-coded against the committed base model (b_tok = 2.2, b_tok/entropy-coded central): K shrinks 9x for the same inference allowance. The auditor's lever. Assumes a public cap on the committed parameters' size, a few times the largest permitted model, proved inside the zero-knowledge proof, so no noise tables or corpora of that size can be committed.

The Oct 17 write-up's K (about 11 MB), with Gamma rescaled so that Kimi K2 inference at 20 bits per token complies as declared: Gamma = K x 2 N_active / b_tok = 2.9e17. The write-up's own Gamma, 9.5e17, is calibrated to Kimi-K3, whose shapes are unconfirmed. Assumes a public cap on the committed parameters' size, a few times the largest permitted model, proved inside the zero-knowledge proof, so no noise tables or corpora of that size can be committed.

The thread draft's dense example: 100B active parameters, smallest inner dimension 3072, e = 49152 (the draft's 7168 is false: one MLP input value multiplies the up projection's 4 x 12288 weights); K = 2e7, Gamma = 2 N D at 1M tokens. Assumes a public cap on the committed parameters' size, a few times the largest permitted model, proved inside the zero-knowledge proof, so no noise tables or corpora of that size can be committed.
